findings.description: Truncation MECHANISM mismatch, both directions surfacing the same underspecified gap. SHEET-PUB-002's phrasing ('writes the new range AND truncates the residual tail to the exact row count') reads as two bundled operations that require knowing a 'before' state to identify what's 'residual' — and all three A-outputs (A1, A2, A3) independently converged on exactly that reading: each invents a `prior_row_count`/`previous_row_count` parameter that must be tracked/passed by the caller, plus a CONDITIONAL second truncate/clear sub-request emitted only `if previous_row_count > new_count`. The real `SheetsViewClient` trait's write method — `fn batch_update_view(&mut self, tab: &ViewTab) -> Result<(), ViewError>` (sheets-view/src/lib.rs) — carries no such parameter anywhere, and the real adapter (`ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view` in runtime/src/adapters.rs) issues exactly ONE unconditional `self.api.update_range(&Self::data_range(&tab.name), &grid)` call against a fixed, open-ended range `'{name}'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z` — no branch on old vs. new row count exists at all. The InMemorySheetsView test fake makes this explicit: truncation is achieved by unconditionally replacing the whole row vector (`existing.rows = tab.rows.clone(); // tail-truncate: wholesale replace`), never by comparing counts. So: A invents a stateful, diff-based truncate design that traces to the spec's literal wording but has zero counterpart in the real trait/tests; B (reading the code) reveals the real mechanism is stateless and unconditional. Neither the spec's implied 'compare to prior, truncate the difference' model nor the reason the code gets away without it is ever stated in the EARS text — the requirement text underdetermines which of these two materially different implementations is intended.

Frozen-header immutability via unconditional hard assertion — code-side surplus SHEET-PUB-002 never states. All three B reconstructions (B1-UB2, B2, B3) capture that a republish presenting a header different from the tab's first-published header is a hard contract violation. The real enforcement, in `InMemorySheetsView::batch_update_view` (sheets-view/src/testkit.rs), is `assert_eq!(existing.header, tab.header, "the frozen header must never be rewritten on republish")` — an unconditional panic in every build, deliberately not release-stripped (per the surrounding comment). SHEET-PUB-002's text is entirely about the data range's write+truncate; it says nothing about header mutability, let alone that a mismatch should panic rather than, say, silently keep the old header or return an error.

Fixed addressing constants pinned by code and tests, absent from spec text. `DATA_START_ROW = 2` (sheets-view/src/lib.rs) and the hard column bound to `Z` in `'{tab}'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z` (runtime/src/adapters.rs `ViewSheetsAdapter::data_range`) are exercised directly — e.g. `runtime/tests/adapters.rs::view_republish_and_marks_read_back_ride_the_one_primitive` asserts `DATA_START_ROW == 2` and that the header row's `Symbol` cell survives a republish untouched, proving the write starts exactly at row 2. SHEET-PUB-002 says only 'the new range' — it never anchors a start row or bounds a column, leaving both entirely to the implementation. All three B-outputs (B1-U1, B2, B3) independently pin this exact constant and range shape.

Low-level batchUpdate JSON/typed-request shape is invented and has no counterpart at the audited layer. All three A-outputs construct literal Sheets API v4 structures (`updateCells`/`UpdateCellsRequest`, `GridRange`, a numeric `sheetId`/`grid_id`) to realize 'single batchUpdate.' The real code never does this at the sheets-view/runtime boundary: `SheetsViewClient::batch_update_view` and its real `ViewSheetsAdapter` implementation route through one opaque call, `SheetsApi::update_range(range: &str, grid: &Grid)`, keyed by a plain string tab name, not a numeric grid/sheet id, and never touch a `Request`/`GridRange` type. This is a secondary facet of the same invented-mechanism gap as the truncation-conditional finding above (both stem from A assuming the crate itself speaks the literal Sheets v4 batchUpdate wire format, when in the real code that concern is pushed down into a lower, unshown primitive).

Missing-tab bootstrap (create-implies-write) sequence — code-side elaboration adjacent to, but outside, SHEET-PUB-002's stated scope. All three B-outputs capture the real `ensure_sheet` → write header once → write data sequence for a not-yet-existing tab (runtime/src/adapters.rs `ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view`'s `is_missing_tab` branch). SHEET-PUB-002's text is scoped to rewriting an EXISTING tab's residual tail; it says nothing about tab-creation bootstrap. Likely belongs to a neighboring EARS ID, but B's code-only vantage naturally folded it in.

notes: Read the 5 given files in full (sheets-view/src/lib.rs, sheets-view/src/testkit.rs, sheets-view/tests/republish.rs, runtime/src/adapters.rs, runtime/tests/adapters.rs) before classifying. Key ground truth: `SheetsViewClient::batch_update_view(&mut self, tab: &ViewTab) -> Result<(), ViewError>` takes no prior-row-count state; the real adapter issues exactly one `update_range` call to the fixed open-ended range `'{name}'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z` (DATA_START_ROW=2); truncation in the test fake is an unconditional full-vector replace (`existing.rows = tab.rows.clone()`), never a size comparison; the frozen header is enforced by an unconditional `assert_eq!` panic in `InMemorySheetsView::batch_update_view`. A-direction agreement is high: all three (A1/A2/A3) independently invent the same `prior_row_count`-tracked, conditionally-branching two-request design and the same literal Sheets v4 JSON/Request scaffolding, differing only in minor surface details (column-width scoping, exact field masks). B-direction agreement is high: all three (B1/B2/B3) independently pin DATA_START_ROW=2/'A2:Z', the hard-assert frozen-header contract, the single-call/wholesale-replace truncation mechanism, the missing-tab bootstrap sequence, and the surrounding stale/lock/tab-order/settle-pass machinery, with B2 additionally supplying the most granular PriceReading column-parsing rules (a B2-only elaboration, not central to SHEET-PUB-002). No direction showed internal disagreement severe enough to call INCONSISTENT-BLIND.
